facts.text: I read that Division I college football players in many schools devote twelve minutes a day to practicing meditation for stress relief.
I have serious back pain.
I was told by a heart doctor that I had a high vagal tone, common among serious athletes.
I have been through a recent crisis despite having a high vagal tone.
I wanted to be more resilient after reading that one person may be thirty times as resilient as another.
I thought it would not be so bad to be thirty times as resilient as other kids.
I wanted stress management to enhance my resilience, meaning the ability to switch quickly from the sympathetic to the parasympathetic nervous system.
I used to think slow breathing was stupid.
I was told that breathing exercises, especially going slow on the exhale, heighten vagal tone.
I was told that exercise also increases vagal tone.
I read that stress is trainable and that stress-avoidance and mindfulness will help at some level.
I ended up editing chapter 11 of an original book for the last time.
An obituary in the New York Times for John E. Sarno, MD appeared on the day the chapter was edited.
John E. Sarno, MD wrote the book Healing and Back Pain.
The New York Times described John E. Sarno, MD as “revered by some as a saint and dismissed by others as a quack.”
I asked whether the user knew chapter 11 of the original book.
I told the other person to read the chapter 11 of the original book that I sent and save it in memory.
I asked the other person to continue the text of chapter 11 of the new book as much as they like based on the provided chapter 11 text and their own information.
I asked for the continuation to be explained with deep learning to me as if I were 10 years old.
I asked that the text be completely scientific and academic and based on science.
I asked to avoid repetition in the writing.
I asked to write each chapter for ten A5 pages.
I asked to classify the contents of chapter 11 into ten sections.
I asked that for each of the ten parts, the other person produce ten pages of content or twenty paragraphs that are not repetitive and related to the topic.
I told the other person that the chapter I gave is just a starting point and they have the right to add relevant foliage.
I asked the other person to start based on chapter 11 of the original book.
